questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is a federal system of government?

options.A: A system where all powers are concentrated in the central authority
options.B: A system in which governmental powers are constitutionally divided between a central authority and regional units
options.C: A system where regional units have the right to secede
options.D: A system where the Constitution is created by agreement among sovereign states

questions.explanation: A federal system is one in which governmental powers are constitutionally divided between a central authority and regional units, with each level exercising powers assigned to it by the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article describes India as a Union of States?
questions.explanation: Article 1 describes India, that is Bharat, as a Union of States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What exact expression does Article 1 use for India?

options.A: India shall be a Federation of States
options.B: India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States
options.C: India shall be a Quasi-Federal State
options.D: India shall be a Confederation of States

questions.explanation: Article 1 uses the expression 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States'.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Why is India described as a Union of States rather than a federation formed by agreement among States?

options.A: Because the Constitution results from an agreement among sovereign States
options.B: Because States have a constitutional right to secede
options.C: Because the Constitution does not result from an agreement among sovereign States and no State has a right to secede
options.D: Because the Union can be dissolved by any State

questions.explanation: The Constitution does not result from an agreement among sovereign States, and no State has a constitutional right to secede from the Union.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who described the Indian Constitution as 'quasi-federal'?
questions.explanation: K. C. Wheare is commonly associated with describing the Indian Constitution as quasi-federal.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a federal feature of the Indian Constitution?

options.D: Appointment of Governors by the President

questions.explanation: A written and supreme Constitution is a federal feature. The others strengthen the Union.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following features strengthens the Union in the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Single citizenship is a unitary feature that strengthens the Union. The others are federal features.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Does India have separate State citizenship in addition to Indian citizenship?
questions.explanation: India follows single citizenship; there is no separate State citizenship.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in specified federal disputes between the Centre and States?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court has original jurisdiction in specified federal disputes under Article 131.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is cooperative federalism?

options.A: A model where States compete with each other
options.B: A model in which the Union and States work together through consultation, coordination and joint institutions
options.C: A model where the Centre exercises absolute control over States
options.D: A model where States have the right to secede

questions.explanation: Cooperative federalism is a model in which the Union and States work together through consultation, coordination and joint institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is competitive federalism?

options.A: A model where the Union and States work together
options.B: A model in which States seek to improve governance, investment and development outcomes in comparison with one another
options.C: A model where the Centre dictates policies to States
options.D: A model where States have unequal powers

questions.explanation: Competitive federalism is a model in which States seek to improve governance, investment, service delivery and development outcomes in comparison with one another.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is asymmetric federalism?

options.A: A federal arrangement where all States have identical powers
options.B: A federal arrangement in which certain States or regions receive different constitutional arrangements or special provisions
options.C: A federal arrangement where the Centre has no power
options.D: A federal arrangement based on population

questions.explanation: Asymmetric federalism is a federal arrangement in which certain States or regions receive different constitutional arrangements or special provisions to address distinct circumstances.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Articles contain special provisions for specified States reflecting asymmetric federalism?
questions.explanation: Articles 371 to 371J contain special provisions for specified States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Schedules provide special arrangements for Scheduled Areas and tribal areas, reflecting asymmetric federalism?
questions.explanation: The Fifth and Sixth Schedules provide special arrangements for Scheduled Areas and tribal areas.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Part of the Constitution primarily deals with relations between the Union and the States?
questions.explanation: Part XI, Articles 245 to 263, primarily deals with relations between the Union and the States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which two broad categories of Centre-State relations are covered in Part XI?
questions.explanation: Part XI covers legislative relations under Articles 245 to 255 and administrative relations under Articles 256 to 263.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Where are Centre-State financial relations primarily provided?
questions.explanation: Centre-State financial relations are primarily provided in Part XII, Articles 264 to 293.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Schedule distributes legislative subjects between the Union and the States?
questions.explanation: The Seventh Schedule distributes legislative subjects between the Union and the States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How many lists are contained in the Seventh Schedule?
questions.explanation: The Seventh Schedule contains three lists: the Union List, State List and Concurrent List.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article gives the constitutional basis for distribution of legislative subjects through the Seventh Schedule?
questions.explanation: Article 246 gives the constitutional basis for distribution of legislative subjects through the Seventh Schedule.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which list contains subjects of national importance on which Parliament ordinarily legislates?
questions.explanation: The Union List (List I) contains subjects of national importance on which Parliament ordinarily legislates.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which list contains subjects primarily assigned to State Legislatures?
questions.explanation: The State List (List II) contains subjects primarily assigned to State Legislatures.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who has residuary legislative power in India?
questions.explanation: Parliament has residuary legislative power under Article 248 read with Entry 97 of the Union List.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What are residuary subjects?

options.A: Subjects enumerated in the Union List
options.B: Subjects enumerated in the State List
options.C: Subjects not enumerated in the Union, State or Concurrent Lists
options.D: Subjects enumerated in the Concurrent List

questions.explanation: Residuary subjects are subjects not enumerated in the Union, State or Concurrent Lists.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article defines the territorial extent of laws made by Parliament and State Legislatures?
questions.explanation: Article 245 defines the territorial extent of laws made by Parliament and State Legislatures.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the territorial extent of a law made by Parliament?

options.C: The whole or any part of the territory of India
options.D: Only States where it is ratified

questions.explanation: Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of the territory of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the territorial extent of a law made by a State Legislature?

options.B: The whole or any part of that State
options.C: Only the capital of the State

questions.explanation: A State Legislature may make laws for the whole or any part of that State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Can a Parliamentary law be invalid merely because it has extra-territorial operation?

options.B: No, under Article 245(2) such a law is not deemed invalid on that ground
options.C: Only if a State challenges it

questions.explanation: Article 245(2) states that a law made by Parliament shall not be deemed invalid on the ground that it would have extra-territorial operation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article distributes legislative subjects between Parliament and State Legislatures?
questions.explanation: Article 246 distributes legislative subjects between Parliament and State Legislatures.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the general rule for the Union List?

options.B: Both Parliament and State Legislatures share power
options.C: Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on matters in List I

questions.explanation: Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on matters enumerated in List I, subject to the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the general rule for the State List?

options.B: State Legislatures ordinarily have exclusive power over matters in List II

questions.explanation: State Legislatures ordinarily have exclusive power over matters in List II, subject to the Constitution and exceptions allowing Parliament to legislate.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the general rule for the Concurrent List?

options.C: Both Parliament and State Legislatures may legislate, subject to the rule of repugnancy

questions.explanation: Both Parliament and State Legislatures may legislate on matters in List III, subject to the rule of repugnancy and other constitutional provisions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article gives Parliament exclusive power to legislate on residuary matters?
questions.explanation: Article 248 gives Parliament exclusive power to legislate on residuary matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which entry in the Union List deals with residuary matters?
questions.explanation: Entry 97 of List I in the Seventh Schedule deals with residuary matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article gives Parliament power to legislate on State List matters in the national interest when the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution?
questions.explanation: Article 249 gives Parliament power to legislate on State List matters in the national interest when the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What majority is required for a Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249?

options.A: Simple majority of members present and voting
options.C: Not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting
options.D: Three-fourths of members present and voting

questions.explanation: Article 249 requires a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How long does an Article 249 resolution remain in force?

options.B: One year, renewable for further periods of not more than one year each

questions.explanation: An Article 249 resolution remains in force for a period not exceeding one year, but may be renewed for further periods of not more than one year each.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: For how long does a law made by Parliament under Article 249 continue after the resolution ceases to operate?

options.C: Six months after the resolution ceases
options.D: One year after the resolution ceases

questions.explanation: A law made under Article 249 ceases to have effect six months after the resolution ceases, except as regards things done or omitted before then.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article allows Parliament to legislate on State List matters during a Proclamation of National Emergency?
questions.explanation: Article 250 allows Parliament to legislate on State List matters during a Proclamation of National Emergency.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How long does a Parliamentary law made under Article 250 continue after the Emergency ceases?

options.C: Six months after the Proclamation ceases
options.D: One year after the Proclamation ceases

questions.explanation: A law made under Article 250 ceases to have effect six months after the Proclamation ceases, except as regards things done or omitted before then.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article permits Parliament to legislate for two or more States by consent of those States?
questions.explanation: Article 252 permits Parliament to legislate for two or more States by consent of those States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Can a State Legislature unilaterally amend or repeal a law made by Parliament under Article 252?

options.A: Yes, any State can amend it
options.B: No, such a law may be amended or repealed by Parliament only
options.D: Yes, if two or more States agree

questions.explanation: A law made under Article 252 may be amended or repealed by Parliament, and not by the legislatures of the consenting States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article empowers Parliament to legislate to implement international treaties and agreements?
questions.explanation: Article 253 empowers Parliament to legislate to implement international treaties and agreements.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Does Parliament need State consent to make a law under Article 253 to implement an international agreement?

options.A: Yes, consent of all States is required
options.B: Yes, consent of affected States is required
options.C: No, Parliament may legislate for the whole or any part of India to implement treaties

questions.explanation: Parliament may legislate for the whole or any part of India to implement treaties, agreements, conventions or decisions made at international conferences or bodies without State consent.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article deals with inconsistency between Union and State laws on Concurrent List matters?
questions.explanation: Article 254 deals with inconsistency between Union and State laws on Concurrent List matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the general rule when a State law conflicts with a Parliamentary law on a Concurrent List subject?

options.B: The Parliamentary law prevails and the State law is void to the extent of repugnancy
options.D: The Supreme Court decides which prevails

questions.explanation: The Parliamentary law prevails and the State law is void to the extent of repugnancy, subject to Article 254(2).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What happens when a State law on a Concurrent List subject receives the President's assent despite inconsistency with an earlier Parliamentary law?

options.A: The State law is automatically void
options.B: The State law may prevail within that State, but Parliament can later override it

questions.explanation: Under Article 254(2), the State law may prevail within that State, but Parliament can later enact a law overriding, varying or repealing it.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for requirements of recommendation or previous sanction for certain legislative proposals?
questions.explanation: Article 255 addresses requirements as to recommendation and previous sanction, treating specified procedural defects as non-fatal where the required assent is given.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which constitutional situations can Parliament legislate on State List subjects?

options.B: Under Articles 249, 250, 252 and 253, and during President's Rule under Article 356
options.D: Only with the consent of all States

questions.explanation: Parliament can legislate on State List subjects under Articles 249, 250, 252 and 253, and during President's Rule under Article 356, subject to the conditions of each provision.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article enables Parliament to exercise State legislative powers while a State is under President's Rule?
questions.explanation: Article 356, read with the constitutional consequences of the Proclamation, enables Parliament to exercise State legislative powers during President's Rule.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a subject in the Union List?
questions.explanation: Defence is a subject in the Union List. Public order, police and agriculture are in the State List.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a subject in the State List?
questions.explanation: Police is a subject in the State List. Railways, citizenship and banking are in the Union List.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a subject in the Concurrent List?
questions.explanation: Criminal law is a subject in the Concurrent List. Foreign affairs and atomic energy are in the Union List; land revenue is in the State List.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a subject in the Union List?
questions.explanation: Currency is a subject in the Union List. Public health, local government and markets and fairs are in the State List.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a subject in the State List?
questions.explanation: Agriculture is a subject in the State List. Insurance, census and post and telegraphs are in the Union List.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a subject in the Concurrent List?
questions.explanation: Education is a subject in the Concurrent List. Defence and citizenship are in the Union List; police is in the State List.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Amendment Act shifted Education, forests, protection of wild animals and birds, weights and measures, and administration of justice from the State List to the Concurrent List?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 shifted these subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following subjects was shifted from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976?
questions.explanation: Forests were shifted from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976. Police, public order and land revenue remain in the State List.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a subject in the Union List?
questions.explanation: Inter-State trade and commerce is a subject in the Union List. Betting and gambling, State public services and land are in the State List.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a subject in the Concurrent List?
questions.explanation: Marriage and divorce is a subject in the Concurrent List. Railways and atomic energy are in the Union List; public order is in the State List.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Articles primarily deal with administrative relations between the Union and States?
questions.explanation: Articles 256 to 263 in Part XI primarily deal with administrative relations between the Union and States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article requires States to exercise their executive power in a way that ensures compliance with laws made by Parliament?
questions.explanation: Article 256 requires States to exercise their executive power in a way that ensures compliance with laws made by Parliament and allows the Union to give directions for that purpose.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article deals with Union directions to States in specified cases to ensure that State executive power does not impede Union executive power?
questions.explanation: Article 257 provides that State executive power must be exercised so as not to impede or prejudice the exercise of Union executive power, and the Union may give directions for specified purposes.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article allows the Union to give directions to States concerning construction and maintenance of means of communication of national or military importance?
questions.explanation: Article 257(2) allows the Union to give directions to States concerning construction and maintenance of means of communication of national or military importance.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article concerns measures to be taken for protection of railways within a State?
questions.explanation: Article 257(3) concerns measures to be taken for protection of railways within a State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who bears additional costs incurred by a State in carrying out certain Union directions under Article 257?

options.B: The Government of India, as provided under Article 257(4)

questions.explanation: The Government of India bears additional costs under Article 257(4), subject to agreement or determination under the constitutional procedure.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article deals with entrustment of Union functions to States?
questions.explanation: Article 258 deals with entrustment of Union functions to States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 258(1), can the President entrust Union executive functions to a State or its officers?

options.B: Yes, with the consent of the State Government

questions.explanation: Under Article 258(1), the President may, with the consent of a State Government, entrust Union executive functions to that State or its officers.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article permits a State, with the consent of the Government of India, to entrust State functions to the Union?
questions.explanation: Article 258A permits a State, with the consent of the Government of India, to entrust State functions to the Union.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for the jurisdiction of the Union in relation to territories outside India?
questions.explanation: Article 260 provides for the jurisdiction of the Union in relation to territories outside India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for public acts, records and judicial proceedings to be recognised throughout India?
questions.explanation: Article 261 provides that full faith and credit shall be given throughout India to public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and every State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 261 provide regarding public acts, records and judicial proceedings?

options.A: They are valid only in the State of origin
options.B: Full faith and credit shall be given throughout India to them, subject to the manner and conditions provided by law
options.D: They are subject to the approval of the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Article 261 provides that full faith and credit shall be given throughout India to public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and every State, subject to the manner and conditions provided by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-State rivers or river valleys?
questions.explanation: Article 262 provides for adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-State rivers or river valleys.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Can Parliament exclude the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts over inter-State river water disputes under Article 262?

options.B: Yes, Parliament may by law provide that neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall exercise jurisdiction in respect of such disputes
options.C: Only the President can exclude jurisdiction
options.D: Only the Supreme Court can exclude its own jurisdiction

questions.explanation: Article 262 permits Parliament by law to provide that neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall exercise jurisdiction in respect of such disputes, subject to the constitutional and statutory framework.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for an Inter-State Council?
questions.explanation: Article 263 provides for an Inter-State Council.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who may establish an Inter-State Council under Article 263?

options.B: The President, if it appears that public interest would be served by its establishment

questions.explanation: The President may establish an Inter-State Council if it appears that public interest would be served by its establishment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for creation of All-India Services common to the Union and States?
questions.explanation: Article 312 provides for creation of All-India Services common to the Union and States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which House of Parliament must pass a resolution to create a new All-India Service under Article 312?

options.D: A joint sitting of both Houses

questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha must pass a resolution to create a new All-India Service under Article 312.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What majority is required in the Rajya Sabha under Article 312 to create a new All-India Service?

options.B: Not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting

questions.explanation: Not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting must support the resolution under Article 312.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the purpose of All-India Services?

options.A: To provide separate cadres for each State
options.B: To provide a common administrative cadre serving both the Union and State Governments and support administrative coordination and national integration

questions.explanation: All-India Services provide a common administrative cadre serving both the Union and State Governments and support administrative coordination and national integration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Name the principal All-India Services.
questions.explanation: The principal All-India Services are the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS) and Indian Forest Service (IFoS).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Act regulates recruitment and conditions of service of the IAS and IPS?
questions.explanation: The All-India Services Act, 1951 regulates recruitment and conditions of service of the IAS and IPS.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional Articles provide for Public Service Commissions for the Union and States?
questions.explanation: Articles 315 to 323 in Part XIV provide for Public Service Commissions for the Union and States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Part of the Constitution primarily deals with financial relations between the Union and States?
questions.explanation: Part XII, Articles 264 to 293, primarily deals with financial relations between the Union and States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article defines 'taxation' for constitutional purposes?
questions.explanation: Article 366(28) defines taxation to include the imposition of any tax or impost, whether general or local or special.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article prohibits taxation except by authority of law?
questions.explanation: Article 265 states that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 265 state?

options.A: Taxes may be levied at the discretion of the executive
options.B: No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law
options.D: Taxes require approval of the Finance Commission

questions.explanation: Article 265 states that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for the Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts of India and of the States?
questions.explanation: Article 266 provides for the Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts of India and of the States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.B: The fund into which all revenues received by the Government of India, loans raised and loan repayments are credited, with withdrawals requiring appropriation in accordance with law
options.C: A fund managed by the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: A fund for development projects only

questions.explanation: The Consolidated Fund of India is the fund into which all revenues received by the Government of India, loans raised by it and money received in repayment of loans are credited; withdrawals require appropriation in accordance with law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the Contingency Fund of India?

options.B: A fund under Article 267 placed at the disposal of the President to enable advances for unforeseen expenditure pending legislative authorisation
options.C: A fund managed by the Finance Commission

questions.explanation: The Contingency Fund of India is a fund under Article 267 placed at the disposal of the President to enable advances for unforeseen expenditure pending legislative authorisation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for Contingency Funds of India and States?
questions.explanation: Article 267 provides for Contingency Funds of India and States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the Public Account of India?

options.A: The fund into which all revenues are credited
options.B: An account under Article 266(2) for money received by or on behalf of the Government other than revenues, public loans and loan repayments
options.D: A fund managed by the Reserve Bank of India

questions.explanation: The Public Account of India is an account under Article 266(2) for money received by or on behalf of the Government of India other than revenues, public loans and loan repayments; the government acts in a fiduciary or banking capacity for such funds.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article deals with duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States?
questions.explanation: Article 268 deals with duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article deals with service tax or other specified duties levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States?
questions.explanation: Article 269 deals with service tax or other specified duties levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States, read with GST-related amendments and Article 269A.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article deals with taxes on inter-State trade or commerce in goods and services under the GST framework?
questions.explanation: Article 269A provides for levy and collection of GST on supplies in the course of inter-State trade or commerce, including imports, with apportionment between the Union and States as provided by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article empowers Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws on GST, with Parliament having exclusive power over inter-State supplies?
questions.explanation: Article 246A empowers Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws on GST; Parliament has exclusive power over inter-State supplies under Article 246A(2).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for the GST Council?
questions.explanation: Article 279A provides for the GST Council.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who is the Chairperson of the GST Council?
questions.explanation: The Union Finance Minister is the Chairperson of the GST Council.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who are the other principal members of the GST Council?

options.A: The Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance and the Minister in charge of Finance or Taxation of each State
options.B: The Chief Ministers of all States
options.D: The Finance Secretaries of all States

questions.explanation: The other principal members are the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance and the Minister in charge of Finance or Taxation, or another nominated Minister, of each State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for taxes levied and distributed between the Union and States, subject to constitutional exclusions and the GST framework?
questions.explanation: Article 270 provides for taxes levied and distributed between the Union and States, subject to constitutional exclusions and the GST framework.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for grants-in-aid from the Union to certain States?
questions.explanation: Article 275 provides for grants-in-aid from the Union to certain States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article permits the Union or a State to make grants for any public purpose?
questions.explanation: Article 282 permits the Union or a State to make grants for any public purpose.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the difference between statutory grants and discretionary grants?

options.A: Statutory grants are under Article 282; discretionary grants are under Article 275
options.B: Statutory grants are provided under constitutional or statutory requirements such as Article 275; discretionary grants may be made for public purposes under Article 282
options.D: Statutory grants require State consent; discretionary grants do not

questions.explanation: Statutory grants are provided under constitutional or statutory requirements, such as Article 275; discretionary grants may be made for public purposes under Article 282, subject to law and budgetary authorisation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for the Finance Commission?
questions.explanation: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who constitutes the Finance Commission?
questions.explanation: The President of India constitutes the Finance Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How often is the Finance Commission ordinarily constituted?

options.B: Every five years, or earlier if the President considers it necessary

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission is ordinarily constituted every five years, or earlier if the President considers it necessary.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who appoints the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission?

options.B: The President, under Article 280 and the Finance Commission Act, 1951

questions.explanation: The President appoints the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission under Article 280 and the Finance Commission Act, 1951.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the principal function of the Finance Commission?

options.B: To recommend the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and States and the allocation among States of their respective shares

questions.explanation: The principal function of the Finance Commission is to recommend the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and States and the allocation among States of their respective shares.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is vertical devolution?

options.A: Distribution of the States' share among individual States
options.B: Distribution of the divisible pool of central taxes between the Union and all States as a group
options.C: Distribution of taxes between Panchayats and Municipalities
options.D: Distribution of GST between the Union and States

questions.explanation: Vertical devolution is the distribution of the divisible pool of central taxes between the Union and all States as a group.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is horizontal devolution?
